A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain 39 pages, including Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, figures and qualitative examples are readable and reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original VL-adaptation and safety-tuning experiments, safety/helpfulness measurements, weight-merging experiments and appendix ablations (Tables 1–7; Figures 2–9).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark measurements, representation analyses, merging ablations and qualitative model outputs.

M1.justification: The VL-adaptation, safety SFT/DPO, SPPFT and weight-merging procedures are unchanged. Section 6.2 retains the same merging formula and selected 0.4/0.6 weighting of the safety-tuned and Chatty models.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same adaptation and safety-training datasets, safety/helpfulness benchmarks and qualitative scenarios. The additional knowledge-domain evaluations in Appendix D and examples in Appendix F are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including SFT, DPO and SPPFT variants, TIES/DARE merging in Table 3, and the open-source LVLMs in Table 5. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and Appendices A–C retain identical model configurations, filtering procedures, training budgets, evaluation metrics and checkpoint evaluation procedures. No experimental protocol is introduced or revised.

E4.justification: The representation analyses, merging-ratio and merging-method ablations, base-model and frozen-layer analyses, and Appendix F qualitative cases are unchanged. The new Section 4.3 heading introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout both PDFs. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative outputs match across both versions, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 54.4% average text-only ASR for LLaMA-2-Chat-VL; no result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The merging equation and combined safety/helpfulness score in Section 6.2 are identical. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, derivation or proof is added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about safety degradation despite filtered training data, safety/helpfulness trade-offs, and weight merging as a balancing approach. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The safety-layer and divergent-objective interpretations remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning architecture coverage, model compatibility and unexplored biases. The Section 4.3 heading summarizes an RLHF limitation already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C preserve the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, timing, evaluation instructions and layer-analysis procedures. Code/model/data access statements and link targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations and bibliography are unchanged. Both versions position the study identically relative to prior LVLM safety research and model-merging methods.

P1.justification: v2 adds the heading '4.3 RLHF Still Faces Limitations in the Safety-Helpfulness Trade-off' before existing discussion. It also changes 'Naver' to 'NAVER' and removes the conference-publication running header. Substantive prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The running-header text is removed, and the added Section 4.3 heading causes limited reflow on pages 6–10, including vertical shifts of Figures 5–6. Figures and tables retain their designs, contents and captions.

improvement.justification: The new Section 4.3 heading makes the existing RLHF discussion easier to locate, while the other edits concern header and affiliation presentation. Methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
